  <entry>
    <id>https://onlinegoddess.net/2026/07/re-why-i-left-wordpress-for-bearblog/</id>
    <title>Re: Why I Left Wordpress for BearBlog</title>
    <updated>2026-07-29T17:05:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>onlinegoddess</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;I saw Paul’s post &lt;a href='https://catsandbirdsandstuff.com/why-i-left-wordpress-for-bearblog/' target='_blank'&gt;Why I Left Wordpress for BearBlog&lt;/a&gt; a little earlier today. As a fellow Wordpress refugee who has been using it for almost 2 decades, for both personal and work purposes, I decided to reply with my own thoughts.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Like Paul says, the key problem is it’s pretty bloated and now seems to be jack of all trades, but master of none. The recent push to incorporate AI functionality into core has only lowered my opinion of it further. That and the petty leadership that has made itself known over the last couple of years &lt;sup class="footnote-ref" id="fnref-1"&gt;&lt;a href="#fn-1"&gt;1&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I was very happy to migrate to Bear for my personal blog. I had over 200 posts, which took me quite some time to bring over. A lot of the old links don’t work, sadly because they simply don’t exist anymore. I guess that’s what happens when you’ve been blogging since 2001.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Unfortunately I’m still stuck with it for work. We use Woocommerce because it does exactly what we need it to do and we’re not reliant on a marketplace that could take us offline at any moment. Initially, we started on Etsy, but seeing other sellers get pulled for alleged  T&amp;C breaches and/or having payments withheld (often with limited recourse) was deeply concerning.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Wordpress has the benefit of being usable on any host you like, and therefore within whatever budget you have. If you don’t like the hosting company anymore, you can simply download a backup and move on.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The bloat is something we struggle with as it’s out of our control. We also need a huge amount of plugins to have our shop function. As of writing this, there are 50 active plugins running:&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The ones we &lt;em&gt;choose&lt;/em&gt; to use:&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Woocommerce (our e-commerce platform)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Blocksy Companion (required to use our theme to full potential)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Advanced Shipment Tracking Pro (adds new shipping statuses so customers can see where their order is after dispatch)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Trackship for WC (integration with Trackship and AST for package tracking)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Newsletter + 11 subplugins (our newsletter and multiple add-on functions)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Site Reviews + 5 subplugins (automatically requests reviews from customers and allows photo uploads)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Reserved Stock Pro (allows customers to reserve an item for a fixed time, preventing oversells)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Countdown Block (for giving advanced notice of product launches)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Fluent Snippets (so I can add code without directly editing core files)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Fluent SMTP (so we can send transactional emails reliably)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Logtivity (for error tracking)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Perfmatters (enables tweaking of Wordpress/Woocommerce to improve performance)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Shortcodes to Show/Hide Content (lets us schedule content to appear at specific times)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Simple CAPTCHA with Cloudflare Turnstile (helps prevent spam accounts and fake orders)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Stock Status for WC (lets us configure custom stock statuses)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The ones that &lt;em&gt;should&lt;/em&gt; be built-in to Wordpress or Woocommerce by default:&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Two factor authentication (frankly necessary for admin, especially on a shop!)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Bulk remove posts from category (can’t believe this isn’t possible by default)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Redirection (it’s so basic, why do I need a plugin for this?)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Disable media sizes (stops Wordpress resizing images by default)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Real-time Find and Replace (changes text strings through the site)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;WC Update Manager (required for Woocommerce plugins to auto-update)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Yaycurrency (allows the shop to display prices in multiple currencies)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Customs Fees for WC (required for taking orders from the EU)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Flexible Shipping (for setting up shipping costs per country)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Fluent Forms (so customers can contact us)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;PDF Invoices and Packing Slips + 2 subplugins (for creating professional invoices)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;WC PayPal Payments (allows us to take PayPal payments)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Product Customer List for WC (shows a list of which customers bought a given product)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The ones we’re &lt;em&gt;forced&lt;/em&gt; to use by our host (Wordpress.com):&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Akismet (I don’t accept comments, but have to keep this anti-spam plugin installed).&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Jetpack + 2 subplugins (an absolute resource hog that inserts itself everywhere. I’ve disabled pretty much all settings except for backups, but the plugin remains).&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Of all these plugins, we have ongoing annual subscriptions for 9 of them and made a one-off payment for 1 other. So it’s not just a case of hosting and domain fees, it’s necessary for us to pay another few hundred pounds a year to obtain the functionality we need for a smoothly-run shop. I can see the appeal of marketplaces like Shopify when it comes to this, as they tend to include all functionality under one subscription. And they don’t suffer from one other huge worry…&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Updating.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Occasionally a plugin will cause breaking changes after updating and then I have to hunt down whatever it’s suddenly become incompatible with. The more plugins used, the more likely this is to happen.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Paul mentions that Wordpress feels more like a content creation tool now. As a business, that kind of fits our needs, but I am very sensitive to the unnecessary collection of data and shoving unwanted dickovers &lt;sup class="footnote-ref" id="fnref-2"&gt;&lt;a href="#fn-2"&gt;2&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt; etc in customers faces. I’m quite proud to say our shop doesn’t need a cookie banner because we simply don’t use &lt;strong&gt;any&lt;/strong&gt; non-essential ones, and I wrote a simple cookie policy that explains the ones we do use and why:&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Shopping&lt;/strong&gt;: These help remember your shopping basket and account status.
&lt;em&gt;These cookies contain “wordpress”, “wp”, “woocommerce”, “fragments” or “cart” in their name.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Payment&lt;/strong&gt;: These ensure you can make payment and appear when you’re logged in.
&lt;em&gt;These cookies contain “PayPal”, “PPCP” or “pay.google” in their name.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Sessions&lt;/strong&gt;: These retain temporary data such as logged-in status.
&lt;em&gt;These cookies contain “session”, or similar, in their name.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Preferences&lt;/strong&gt;: These remember your settings preferences, such as light/dark mode, selected currency etc.
&lt;em&gt;These cookies contain “blocksy” or “currency”&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Anyway the crux of it is, I’d &lt;em&gt;love&lt;/em&gt; to leave Wordpress behind for good, but for work it’s just not an option at the moment. In the meantime, I’ll keep our shop looking as lean and clean as I possibly can, no thanks to Wordpress.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Hey &lt;a href='https://herman.bearblog.dev' target='_blank'&gt;Herman&lt;/a&gt;, any interest in starting Bearcommerce? 😄&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;hr /&gt;

&lt;blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Cheers for the mention on your blog! Flattered to have started the conversation. Having seen your list of 50 plugins, I think you've made my case against WordPress far better than I did.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;ul&gt;

&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Footnotes&lt;/strong&gt;:&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;section class="footnotes"&gt;
&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li id="fn-1"&gt;&lt;p&gt;The co-founder and CEO of Wordpress, Matt Mullenweg, started a protracted and vicious legal dispute with hosting company WP Engine in 2024. It’s a messy situation - if you’ve got an hour with nothing to do, &lt;a href='https://wpvswpe.report' target='_blank'&gt;this will spell it all out for you&lt;/a&gt; in glorious detail.&lt;a href="#fnref-1" class="footnote"&gt;&amp;#8617;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li id="fn-2"&gt;&lt;p&gt;I love this term &lt;a href='https://daringfireball.net/2026/05/what_is_a_dickover' target='_blank'&gt;coined by John Gruber&lt;/a&gt; over at Daring Fireball. It’s as satisfying as the moniker AI slop.&lt;a href="#fnref-2" class="footnote"&gt;&amp;#8617;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

  <entry>
    <id>https://angrybunnyman.com/some-advice-dont-get-your-elbow-tattooed-or-reading-things-that-bother-you/</id>
    <title>Some advice: don't get your elbow tattooed or read things that bother you</title>
    <updated>2026-07-29T21:17:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>angrybunnyman</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;div class="dynamic-title"&gt;Portrait of an ongoing Negotiation&lt;/div&gt;
&lt;div class="nutrition-widget" id="nutritionWidget"&gt;
  &lt;div class="nutrition-content" id="nutritionContent"&gt;
    &lt;h3&gt;Post Nutrition Label&lt;/h3&gt;
    &lt;ul&gt;
      &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Content Type:&lt;/strong&gt; Text &amp; Photos &lt;/li&gt;
      &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Read Time:&lt;/strong&gt; 10 min &lt;/li&gt;
      &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Topics:&lt;/strong&gt; Pain, Tattoos, Writing about anything in public&lt;/li&gt;
     &lt;/ul&gt;
  &lt;/div&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I'm having an ongoing conversation with a needle and an artist. The latter I found through a recommendation so many friends-of-friends-of-friends removed that it stopped being a chain and became something closer to causality; it's the universe conspiring to introduce me to the person who'd spend the next decade putting holes in me on purpose.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;This guy has been privy to a lot of pain. This guy has inflicted a lot of pain. I asked him to. He and that needle know something about the elbow joint underneath that I don't, like some old grudge being settled on behalf of every nerve ending unlucky enough to live this close to the surface. Tattoo artists have to be sadists and therapists and gentle parents all at once, sometimes within the same ninety seconds.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h2 id=all-elbows&gt;All elbows&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;Thin skin here linked straight to an internal oh-fuck-ometer that I did not know I had until it started reporting live from the scene. Everyone tells you this before you sit down, like it's a warning you might actually use.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;(It is not and you will not.)&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Thin skin means the artist and his machine aren't just drawing on you as much as they're negotiating directly with the skeleton.Which has Opinions about being negotiated with, none of them charitable. I watch his hand move in that steady metronome way — dip, stab, wipe, dip, stab, wipe — and somewhere around minute eleven my brain, offered nothing to chew on but the specific white-hot arithmetic of &lt;em&gt;this hurts, this hurts,&lt;/em&gt; goes looking for anywhere else to be. Eleven folds into some horrible multiple of itself. It wanders off toward thinking about the thinking, un-experiencing the experience even as it's happening... you know, so I can write about it later. Experience is nothing, these days, if not fodder for the vast crawling internet, one more offering left on an altar that neither says thank you nor stops being hungry. This is what a mind does when you give it nothing but pain to work with: it goes looking for an argument. Any argument.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The one it dredges up, roughly: people are furious that other people keep blogging things. Not bad things — what would "bad" even mean here — just things that don't clear some invisible bar marked &lt;em&gt;useful.&lt;/em&gt; And "useful" is doing a lot of work in that sentence too. I write the way I get tattooed: as a means to my own succor, my own quiet self-made ceremony. These needles are chiseling memory into skin the same way these words are being chiseled into the surface of some server, somewhere, humming in a windowless room I will never see.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h2 id=the-tattoos&gt;The tattoos&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;div class="gallery"&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;img src="https://bear-images.sfo2.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/angrybunnyman/img_5765.webp" alt="IMG_5765" /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;img src="https://bear-images.sfo2.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/angrybunnyman/img_5764.webp" alt="IMG_5764" /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The quick tour, for anyone still with me:&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Newest, just above the blue and yellow syringes — an abstracted accessibility symbol, its wheel framing a bear claw. Guess which came first, the claw or the life-history bands wrapped around it.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Before that, a length of rope for the years spent in community education and leadership, and for a defunct side hustle called Bunnyrope that only a handful of people will ever have reason to remember.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;A stylized focus ring, styled after Canon's branding, though my camera has always been a Nikon. My wife shoots Canon. This one's less for me than for her.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The elbow itself is a shutter set to roughly f/6.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Color goes in come September. Another appointment. Another small negotiated apocalypse.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h2 id=but-what-does-it-meeeeeean&gt;But what does it meeeeeean&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;These marks are, ultimately, meaningless to anyone but me, even too the sparks of pain that came bundled with acquiring them.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;But is that actually true, my All Reading Eye? Do they carry nothing beyond what they mean to me alone? They let you glimpse how the machinery behind this writing is put together Flawed, self-involved, strange... but a machinery all the same. And give a little more flesh to whoever's been narrating at you this whole time. If you find any value in that, why would you value it any less than writing that's shorter, plainer, less feral with its own imagery? Not everything has to be &lt;em&gt;full&lt;/em&gt; — whatever full is even supposed to mean — to still say something true between one mind and another. Sometimes it's a glimpse instead of four fully fleshed ideas etched into skin like a well-worn metaphor. (Pun very much intended.)&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Here's what I'm thinking, at this exact moment, in this exact chair: that I have volunteered a foot and a half of unarmored meat to stinging metal. I knew this walking in. Everybody who's ever gotten an elbow piece knows it walking in.  It's the tattoo equivalent of a warning label nobody reads or heeds. I sat down anyway. I chose the shop. I chose the day. I chose the exact hour where I'd have nothing left to do but marinate in it, alone with the needle and whatever thoughts it summoned up out of me.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h2 id=you-always-have-choice&gt;You always have choice&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;Nobody made me choose this. And you don't have to find any value in that fact, or even stick around long enough to reach this sentence and decide. It carries its weight regardless if you read all of it, some of it, or none of it, and regardless of what you make of it once you have.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;So here's what walking out of the chair would have cost me: an unfinished piece, a wasted deposit, a hole blown clean through an afternoon I'll never get back, and an artist who did nothing wrong left standing there with a needle raised at a man who apparently reconsidered consequences halfway through living them. That is not the same category of cost as closing a browser tab. But there's a whole strain of internet-brain that treats &lt;em&gt;I saw a blog post I didn't need&lt;/em&gt; as though it belongs on the same ledger as &lt;em&gt;pain I did not consent to&lt;/em&gt;, as if scrolling past somebody's diary entry about their cat, their diet, their fourth attempt at re-explaining the same grief in a slightly different arrangement of words, is violence enacted upon the reader rather than a door the reader walked up to, opened themselves, and then stood inside complaining about the draft.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The part the discourse keeps forgetting: you can always leave the chair. The tab closes with less effort than it took to open it. Nobody bolted you to that sentence. Nobody's coming to collect a debt if you never finish reading a post that was never, in the first place, truly written for you.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The wrap goes on around hour four. Vaseline sheen, plastic film, the whole arm throbbing underneath it with a heat that's settled into something closer to a low, even hum. It'll ache worse tomorrow. It'll peel in about a week, itch in that specific maddening way skin itches while it's busy becoming something else entirely, and I won't, go looking for whose fault it is. There isn't a whose. There's just the choice, sitting there afterward, plain as the ink laid into it.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;
&lt;hr&gt;

  <entry>
    <id>https://moodywarlock.net/soaking-in-the-slop/</id>
    <title>Soaking in the slop</title>
    <updated>2026-07-30T02:08:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>moodywarlock</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;We're in a post-ai time. At least, it feels that way. There was a time when nobody was talking about it, and now it's everywhere - saturated feeds, ai music, ai photos, vibe coding. I'm completely sick of it. I know it's being pushed as inevitable and &lt;em&gt;the next stage in human evolution&lt;/em&gt; because some socially awkward, bored, power-hungry billionaires are trying to reshape the world as they see fit and make even more coin. Only one thing is inevitable, and it's not ai.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Should it generate dismay in artists? Possibly. Generative ai is a global grift where copyrighted stuff has been ingested for free so billionaires can sell it back to us. Ai is a way to absorb human skill and produce dependency for profit and control. I'm aware of productive uses of ai-type systems, but this proliferation of large language models, chatbots, art generators, and anthropomorised llms is an insincere scam designed to funnel money and power into the hands of a few.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;So, let them soak in the ai slop. Let them be saturated with hallucinated facts and garbage. The only positive I see is that artists might create their own cottage industry and shun ai in favour of authentic connection. As for me, I cannot abide it. I do art for myself. Those who view art as outcomes to be sold are blind to the time, the failures, the struggle, the learning, the journey, the story, and the human connection that's also part of art. Depending on ai not only serves profit motives, it also shortcuts the art journey to get to the end product to be sold.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I read about one person who'd always wanted to be a music producer and now he's using ai music generators to make music. So, what had he been doing for the last decade? Why not just take time to dig in and learn? Of course, ai is the convenience machine that reduces sweat, toil, time, and failure - all the roughly textured stuff that provides meaning in life to people who understand art.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Let them soak in the slop. Let them marinate in the urine of spiritless billionaires. Let them smoothe their brains and hollow out their eyes. Let them become dependent idiots who feed uncaring tech-lords. Let them short-cut their way to meaninglessness.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href='&amp;#109;&amp;#97;&amp;#105;&amp;#108;&amp;#116;&amp;#111;&amp;#58;&amp;#109;&amp;#111;&amp;#111;&amp;#100;&amp;#121;&amp;#119;&amp;#97;&amp;#114;&amp;#108;&amp;#111;&amp;#99;&amp;#107;&amp;#64;&amp;#112;&amp;#114;&amp;#111;&amp;#116;&amp;#111;&amp;#110;&amp;#46;&amp;#109;&amp;#101;?subject=Soaking in the slop&gt;Email me about this post&lt;/a&gt;. Subscribe to my blog via &lt;a href='/feed/'&gt;RSS feed&lt;/a&gt;. Find me on &lt;a href='https://social.lol/@moodywarlock' target='_blank'&gt;Mastodon&lt;/a&gt; and &lt;a href='https://bsky.app/profile/moodywarlock.bsky.social' target='_blank'&gt;Bluesky&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;img src="https://bear-images.sfo2.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/moodywarlock/written-by-a-human-not-by-ai-badge-white.webp" alt="Written-By-a-Human-Not-By-AI-Badge-white" /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  <entry>
    <id>https://blog.aracine.net/goodbye/</id>
    <title>Goodbye Tech</title>
    <updated>2026-07-30T14:22:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>doesnmatter</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;&lt;img src="https://bear-images.sfo2.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/doesnmatter/rat.webp" alt="rat" /&gt;
&lt;em&gt;Every tech company is different, every tech company is the same. Welcome to the suck.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Yeah no. I'm out.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Of course it's generative AI. Not the tech. The social phenomenon and the mass hysteria of the managerial class. They jumped at the slightest whiff of being able to cut staff, cut costs, cut corners. The unavoidable end of the tech industry McKinsification. It's not new tho. The only thing the average tech company managed to do with every subsequent silver bullet is shoot themselves in the foot. Object Oriented Programming will save us! Now it's agile! The future is big data, wait no, it's blockchain! At every turn, not grasping that the problem was cultural and not that they weren't copying the latest Silicon Valley trend.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;hr /&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Younger, the web represented the new frontier, the democratization of knowledge and entrepreneurship. The barrier of entry was having an internet connection and a laptop. Of course, the newly minted mega corps of the early 00s just sucked everything that was good about it. Growth at all cost and all that. Actual bots -- or human acting like bots -- pleasing algorithms for a quick buck killed the Internet in the mid 2010s. LLMs, like a super bacteria, finished the job and picked the bones clean. Going on the commercial internet is now a source of pain, a labyrinth of dark patterns and traps.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I am grateful I entered the industry at the tail end of its golden age. Still riding the hyper growth wave of early internet and early mobile. I got to make a lot of money doing what I was already doing in my free time since I was a kid. When I started working, I had no quip calling my job software engineering. Now, I don't remember the last time I got to solve actual problems for a user. The industry is more interested in building companies than building products. The inextricable march toward a fully realized mix of Gervais and Peter principle.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I mourn our collective loss of the digital realm to corporate interests. I don't mourn being obligated to use shit products from shit companies because some business idiot decided he needed to do &lt;em&gt;something&lt;/em&gt;. Goodbye Jira, Chrome, and Windows, and every other piece of crap SaaS that adds to the true cost of my employment. I was able to ship in spite of them, not because.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Although I'm stopping selling my particular software and product making skills, I am not breaking up with tech entirely. I will continue fostering my digital homestead, using and hosting software that respects me and solve my issues. I still want to write code, slowly, mostly by hand. I already type syntax as fast as my understanding of the things I'm building grows. Doing the thing is doing the thing and no amount of delegating makes you better at it.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;As for money and not dying of hunger, I'm switching to providing something closer to real human needs. I am not fooling myself than the grass is greener there. Not even close to inflated software salaries and miles harder on the body. More hours too and still working with other humans, some of them ego full idiots. But hey, at least I won't be dealing with self imposed idiosyncrasies and make belief problems anymore. With blameless culture, accountability washing and ritualistic meetings to share information that should easily be surfaced with project management tools.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;So long tech industry, I am happy that you can now go faster toward the wall your were already speeding toward before generative AI. I won't be there for the crash.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;o7&lt;/p&gt;
</content>
    <link href="https://blog.aracine.net/goodbye/" rel="alternate"/>
    <published>2026-07-30T14:22:00+00:00</published>
  </entry>
  <entry>
    <id>https://bearlyadiary.bearblog.dev/re-notes-on-overconsumption-and-instead-of-a-self-help-book/</id>
    <title>re: notes on overconsumption and instead of a self help book</title>
    <updated>2026-07-29T17:25:04.313193+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>bearlyadiary</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href='https://noahmickel.com/notes-on-overconsumption-and-instead-of-a-self-help-book/'&gt;A great post&lt;/a&gt; made it’s way onto the Trending page today.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I agree with pretty much everything in the post, so don’t expect any hot takes.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Every statement I wrote is made from purely anecdotal thoughts, so don’t take any of this as me preaching to you.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;Let’s go!&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;...but the same is not necessarily true for dubious supplements, self-help books, or overprescriptive planning tools. Only in America can multinational companies explain to people that their true self-actualization will only arise via the purchase of additional consumer goods.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I agree. I feel that as the decades have rolled by, the corporate oligarchy that dominates our species has worked overtime to convince the 99% of us that products (supplements, self-help books, planning tools, etc.) that make our lives more convenient, take care of our needs faster, and remove all friction, are what we want to spend our meager slave wages on.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;This is obviously an unsustainable model for human development. At some point, the only way they’ll make us more “productive” is by replacing us with robots.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Oh, wait...&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Anyway. I am convinced that God &lt;em&gt;did not&lt;/em&gt; create us to live &lt;strong&gt;fast&lt;/strong&gt; lives. Adam and Eve were meant to be gardeners in Eden. That is a notoriously slow occupation.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Productivity, or at least, the extreme ideological version of it, is a modern invention and I think that we’re finally seeing its woeful results on the collective human mind, body, and spirit.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;That being said, I also am someone who loves, at least self-help books and productivity tools, and I’m greatly enjoying &lt;em&gt;Atomic Habits&lt;/em&gt; at the moment. &lt;em&gt;A lot&lt;/em&gt; of these products have meaningfully improved my lifestyle, and not necessarily to make me more productive, but to make me more “intentional”, and &lt;em&gt;for my own sake&lt;/em&gt;. Feel free to cast the first stone if you think that &lt;em&gt;all&lt;/em&gt; such products are the devil’s spawn.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Finding a job that is within a reasonable number of hours that pays the bills is lexically prior to anything a productivity or wellness grifter could sell. Financial precarity under late neofeudalism is no joke, and until basic needs are met, no special secret productivity tool will cure longing.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I agree 100%.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;A company does not love its employees, and looking for cosmic meaning and justice from employment is a fool's errand.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Say it louder for the people in the back!&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Wine nights, gratitude journals, and ice cream dinner (because "I deserve it") are at least orthogonal if not counterproductive to the simple shit.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I agree. I think that the “I deserved this treat” mentality is born of a mind that is overworked. The times in my life where I felt burnt out were also the times that I snacked more just to “feel” something other than dread. Had we more lifestyles that are more &lt;strong&gt;temperate&lt;/strong&gt; (and old word for “healthier” &lt;em&gt;and&lt;/em&gt; “more balanced” that needs to make a comeback), then we would feel content with the simple (and often cheaper), harmless pleasures that nature, community, and life afford.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Purely selfishly, it feels good to take care of other people. Take your friend out to lunch for their birthday. Give the homeless person some cash. Plan an event for your friends to get together. The guy who does things for others is awesome.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I think this is the most important point, for me at least (happened to be the last one too).&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;True, we live in a society dominated by and drowning in cynicism, but if we zoom out from that big picture and zoom into our immediate social circle, we’ll often find that many (if not hopefully all) of those closest to us are not only trustworthy but also &lt;em&gt;&lt;strong&gt;very&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/em&gt; worthy of our best efforts to serve them.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Yes, I used the unsightly verb “to serve”. One thing I learned a few years ago is that, in my incessant pursuit of purpose, meaning, achievement, and self-improvement, I directed &lt;em&gt;all&lt;/em&gt; my thoughts to myself, I “served myself” to the point of becoming depressed from self-obsession.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I think that many if not most people who are depressed (even if this isn’t the main cause of their illness) would greatly benefit from &lt;strong&gt;thinking less about self, and more about others&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;When you worry about how to help and be supportive of others, you tend to worry less about your own needs, especially the &lt;em&gt;needless&lt;/em&gt; ones. You probably experienced this during the honeymoon phase of a romantic relationship. It doesn’t have to turn into an extreme. Again, there is a balance to this principle. You “can’t pour from am empty cup” as the saying goes, but I believe that it is a law of nature, that as the oceans evaporate water to the clouds, the clouds rain it on the mountains, the mountains spring it up to the rivers, and the rivers deliver it back to the ocean, that when we &lt;em&gt;all&lt;/em&gt; focus on giving rather than taking, we all end up feeling more ful&lt;strong&gt;filled&lt;/strong&gt;. Pun intended.&lt;/p&gt;
</content>

    <id>https://notes.jeddacp.com/cocoa-rainbowbridge/</id>
    <title>Cocoa has crossed the rainbow bridge</title>
    <updated>2026-07-29T15:19:08.980259+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>jedda</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;My best friend, my soul dog, &lt;em&gt;my everything&lt;/em&gt;, &lt;strong&gt;Cocoa&lt;/strong&gt;, crossed the rainbow bridge on &lt;strong&gt;July 22, 2026&lt;/strong&gt; between 12:46 - 12:51PM Pacific after a fight with IVDD (where she became paralyzed in 3 of her limbs).&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;img src="https://bear-images.sfo2.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/jedda/cocoachanel.png" alt="Diptych of Cocoa, the dachshund" /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I am swimming in an ocean of grief, barely able to float. Cocoa was deeply intertwined in the fabric of my life and routine. She was my (/our) whole world. I have not fully lived my adult life without her. She was with me for nearly 15 years. Losing her is like losing a limb, the very meaning of my existence.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;They say grief is just love with nowhere to go. I have poured all my love into Cocoa, and so this grief is suffocating me. I &lt;em&gt;just&lt;/em&gt; have to keep reminding myself that she is no longer in pain. &lt;em&gt;She was in so much pain the last 24 hours of her life.&lt;/em&gt; It's my turn to hold on to that pain for her.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;One of these days, I will write about our story. Until then, we'll continue to find ways to commemorate her on our own.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Rest easy, my love. Your mom and I will try to hold down the fort for you. &lt;em&gt;Until we meet again.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
