  <entry>
    <id>https://noahmickel.com/notes-on-overconsumption-and-instead-of-a-self-help-book/</id>
    <title>notes on overconsumption and instead of a self help book</title>
    <updated>2026-07-28T20:29:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>noahmickel</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;I had an acquaintance explain to me that his current income of $200,000 a year salary is insufficient to travel whenever he wants, let alone purchase all the luxuries (two mansions, a Bugatti, a supermodel wife) he needs to be happy. This is a truly sad (let alone misogynistic) perspective on life, but it's a hyperbolic version of the typical argument for every product in modern American capitalism. "Buy my product and you'll feel &lt;x&gt;" is the pitch for every sports car or phone upgrade.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The pathetic nature of luxury overconsumption does not seem to extend, however, into the kinds of things that people assume "make us better." Friends may give sideeye to a 29-year-old when they lease an Audi they can't afford, but the same is not necessarily true for dubious supplements, self-help books, or overprescriptive planning tools. Only in America can multinational companies explain to people that their true self-actualization will only arise via the purchase of additional consumer goods.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I will not rewrite here all the work of Peter and Michael over on "If Books Could Kill", but needless to say the self-help book is an incredible example of how someone can take semi-useful advice and bloat it up to book length. In lieu of every self help book you could purchase, here is a brief list of things that makes my life better than it used to be.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h1 id=instead-of-a-self-help-book-by-a-man-too-busy-to-write-one-and-frankly-couldnt-be-bothered&gt;Instead of a Self-Help Book by A Man Too Busy to Write One (and frankly couldn't be bothered)&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;h3 id=1-find-a-job-thats-tolerable&gt;1. Find a Job that's Tolerable&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;Finding a job that is within a reasonable number of hours that pays the bills is lexically prior to anything a productivity or wellness grifter could sell. Financial precarity under late neofeudalism is no joke, and until basic needs are met, no special secret productivity tool will cure longing. A company does not love its employees, and looking for cosmic meaning and justice from employment is a fool's errand. The same logic applies to the overworked finance bros, who should get a real job that isn't ruining the country and allows time for non-work pursuits.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h3 id=2-actually-care-for-yourself&gt;2. Actually Care for Yourself&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;Drink sufficient water. Consume plenty of protein. Eat Vegetables. Take a one-a-day. Sleep 7-9 hours a night. Drink sparingly. Get exercise.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Wine nights, gratitude journals, and ice cream dinner (because "I deserve it") are at least orthogonal if not counterproductive to the simple shit. I spent too much of my life fantastically overweight, and decided I didn't want to treat myself all the way into adult diabetes. Probably widely applicable advice.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h3 id=3-do-things-offline&gt;3. Do Things Offline&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;Read. Play board games. Host a cocktail party. Learn how to make good coffee at home. Woodwork.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The specific hobby is irrelevant, so much as it is disconnected from the internet. The real-world is lovely, go do something in it.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h3 id=4-buy-less-shit&gt;4. Buy Less Shit&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;People get used to luxuries quickly and it is a pain to maintain piles of stuff. For more information, see &lt;a href='https://www.youhavetoomuchshit.com/'&gt;You Have Too Much Shit&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h3 id=5-be-good-to-others&gt;5. Be Good to Others&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;Purely selfishly, it feels good to take care of other people. Take your friend out to lunch for their birthday. Give the homeless person some cash. Plan an event for your friends to get together. The guy who does things for others is awesome.&lt;/p&gt;
</content>
    <link href="https://noahmickel.com/notes-on-overconsumption-and-instead-of-a-self-help-book/" rel="alternate"/>
    <published>2026-07-28T20:29:00+00:00</published>
  </entry>
  <entry>
    <id>https://questfortori.bearblog.dev/i-cant-stop-thinking-about-majoras-mask/</id>
    <title>I Can't Stop Thinking About Majora's Mask</title>
    <updated>2026-07-28T21:44:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>questfortori</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;&lt;img src="https://i.ibb.co/RwMYLvf/IMG-6716.jpg" alt="Majora Screenshot" /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;When I was 7 years old, I rented The Legend of Zelda: Majora’s Mask from our local video rental store in southern Connecticut. Being a stupid kid, I wasn’t able to figure out how to get out of Clock Town on the first cycle, so I wandered aimlessly, speaking with every resident to see if anyone had an idea of how to stop the world’s imminent doom. Seeing the different trauma responses of everyone in Clock Town gave me a gnawing sense that maybe adults don’t have everything as figured out as I once thought. My own response wasn’t much more noble. In the last few minutes before the moon fell, I cowered alone in the South Clock Town water pool, Deku Link’s shield overhead like a child hiding under bed covers. The moon crashed into the land and all life on it was snuffed out. In a sense, I never stopped thinking about that crushingly-powerless moment when I first truly understood what death was.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I’ve never stopped thinking about Majora’s Mask.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;———  &lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Everyone in Termina has their own reaction to the specter of armageddon, and each one tells you a lot about their worldview. Some deny it entirely, some acknowledge it but go about their work regardless, some lash out in an attempt to wrest control over a force of nature, some become totally dysfunctional, and some still try to escape in hopes that they may be spared. I can’t blame any of them. I have been all of these people at different points in my life. Hell, even in just the past year. Ever since America plunged headlong into fascism, I’ve spent every day trying to figure out how to keep me and my loved ones safe, and every time the dread dawns upon me that substantial change is out of my individual control. What is the more terrible fate - to be totally powerless but accepting of that fact, or to have enough power to potentially do something to help some people, but not enough to save even close to everyone you love?&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;In Clock Town, the people deny the moon will fall and mock those who seek to lessen the damage of the impending catastrophe. In the Southern Swamp, a hateful tyrant imprisons and executes minorities to sate the bloodlust of his supporters who demand a scapegoat for problems out of their control. On Mt. Snowhead, people freezing to death refuse to take action to save their village and instead pray to the memory of their dead leaders for aid which they cannot provide. In the Great Bay, a toxic sea makes life uninhabitable and the people simply await death. In Ikana Canyon, the dead wage pointless forever wars to assert the glory of their perceived tribes. It feels like we are trapped in the same painful cycle, trying desperately to find a way out.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;When Link resets time at the end of each three-day cycle, he does so of his own accord. He doesn’t have a choice if he wishes to live another day and maybe make things right, but he still plays the Song of Time and watches everything he did in the past 72 hours get undone. Can you imagine the pain and guilt he must feel every time he resets time and sees everyone forget him and suffer yet again? Every land he has healed, demon he has slain, every person whose life he has made a little better, all reset back to zero.  &lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Except the masks. If you help someone in need, if you ease the pain in their weary heart enough for them to keep living just a bit longer, you’ll get their mask. And you’ll keep their mask.  When my grandfather entered the twilight of his life, his memory started fading, as it does for many people his age. Seeing someone who has been a pillar of my life start to forget basic things about his family hurt in a way I couldn’t articulate. Did he still remember when I was a kid and I used to help him out in his woodworking workshop? I wish I could have been there for him more, but my family’s response to me coming out as trans made that more difficult. When he finally passed, he left me a box of chisels from his workshop. I still keep them among my other personal tools. I still keep his mask.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;———&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The sidequest to reunite the lost lovers Anju and Kafei leaves an emotional mark on virtually everyone who seeks it out in Majora’s Mask. It requires by far the most effort, planning, and research of the daily lives and motivations of everyone in Clock Town to see it through to the end. Spending the final minutes of the final night in the Stock Pot Inn with Anju is a nerve-wracking experience. As she wordlessly awaiting the return of her fiancé, you wonder if you missed something, did something wrong, or maybe made a mistake in even trying to bring these two together right before their death. But indeed, Kafei returns mere seconds before to moon falls to exchange marriage masks with his beloved. The two take you as the witness to their eternal bond and give you the Couple’s Mask to symbolize it. With an unshakeable resolve, they vow to face the dawn together. Link undoes all of this by playing the Song of Time and has to shoulder the pain of splitting them apart yet again, but he’ll keep their mask.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Taking the Couple’s Mask to the mayor’s office on the first morning has an interesting effect. Inside, politicians are bickering about how to save face about an environmental catastrophe (Which they in part caused out of cruelty and neglect in generations past) instead of doing anything meaningful to help the townspeople survive. Upon seeing the Couple’s Mask, they all stop what they’re doing and are humbled by the weight of the human lives who depend on them. It may not convince all of them, but their squabble is broken up and their priorities are realigned for the better.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;For the past decade I have been trying to convince my mother that the Republican Party she votes for materially causes her own daughter suffering. That they enact wretched cruelty upon their enemies and enrich themselves through corruption on an incomprehensible scale. Part of me wants to believe that any honest person should be able to see that, but every time I am proven wrong by her wall of willful ignorance. I bear my mask to her every time we speak, yet her eyes remain closed. “The moon can’t possibly fall, Victoria, stop worrying about things which won’t happen.”&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I want to believe that people can change if one opens their heart to them. On some level, I need to believe it to convince myself this world is not forever doomed to its cycle of pain and violence. Is it foolish to persist in this side quest when there is no end in sight beyond the inevitable final day? Can some simply not be convinced to flee town? Mother, how much have you contorted your soul to rid yourself of a mask to give to others? Can I not keep your mask when you too are gone?&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;———&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Just before the final fight with Majora, if Link gives away every mask he has obtained from helping others in Termina, Majora will say something: “Let’s play good guys against bad guys… Yes. Let’s play that. Are you ready? You’re the bad guy. And when you’re bad, you just run. That’s fine, right?”  &lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Mg3e6w4RYV4"&gt;I heard someone once hypothesize&lt;/a&gt; that this is referring to the fact that the transformation masks all represent dead people important to their communities. But Link wears them anyway, and never tells their loved ones that they died, essentially puppeting their corpses around and not allowing their loved ones to process their deaths. Majora, seeing a world caught in a cycle of suffering and wishing to put everyone out of their misery, may see Link’s attempts to prolong this cycle in an attempt to break it as cowardly and foolish. Even if Link’s intentions are noble, what gives him the right to deny these people closure? Is it right to lie to someone about something so serious to keep their hope alive for just a bit longer? I don't think lying to loved ones is a good idea except in dire situations is a good idea, but if it means saving a life, then perhaps it can be justified? I still don’t have an answer to that question, especially in times like these where hope is scarce and fleeting.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;But maybe if hope is a good enough reason for Link, then it’s good enough for me, too. I don’t have all the answers - I’m just one woman trying to make do with a broken world. But if I do nothing, nothing will improve, and the moon will crash. Even if it hurts to get up each day and learn of new horrors that break your heart, holding onto hope at all costs is the best option we have. Majora’s Mask is about changing the world bit by bit, giving hope to others even if they forget about it mere days later. It’s about the hope that life is worth living if we make it worth living. The fight for a better world may feel never-ending, but it is worth it for the dawn of a new day.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Remember those you’ve lost, love those close to you that yet live, and you’ll keep their masks.&lt;/p&gt;
</content>
    <link href="https://questfortori.bearblog.dev/i-cant-stop-thinking-about-majoras-mask/" rel="alternate"/>
    <published>2026-07-28T21:44:00+00:00</published>
  </entry>
  <entry>
    <id>https://valerialoves.com/why-didnt-silent-titans-change-the-world/</id>
    <title>Why Didn't Silent Titans Change the World?</title>
    <updated>2026-07-28T14:42:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>valerialoves</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;&lt;img src="https://bear-images.sfo2.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/valerialoves/silent-titans-cover.webp" alt="Silent Titans Cover" /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I have read this book so many times.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;This is one of the most common things you could say about Silent Titans, though I suspect my reason differs from most.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The module’s opening scene places the party, immediately post memory-wipe, on a spiral staircase surrounding a time tornado which acts as the spine to a “quasi-living multidimensional hyper-intelligence from an unimaginably distant future” - one of the titular titans. The titan’s body is hidden via spatial distortion inside of a belltower which itself sits like a mast atop a boat on the sea of time. Beneath the giant bell at the top of the staircase (remember the staircase?) Dr. Hog, an anthropomorphic dandy pig in a silver maiden mask, uses a steampunk fungal clavichord to remotely pilot a hive of subservient silver ants which &lt;em&gt;in turn&lt;/em&gt; dominate the engorged, distended minds of his two tommy-gun-toting ape guards. The apes open fire. There are two doors - one Brass, one Ebony - to your immediate left and right. What do you do?&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href='https://falseparcels.bigcartel.com/product/silent-titans-hardcopy'&gt;“Silent Titans… can be a bit much for some people.”&lt;/a&gt;&lt;br /&gt;
&amp;nbsp; - Patrick Stuart, on this book’s sales page.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;img src="https://bear-images.sfo2.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/valerialoves/brunan-spread.webp" alt="Brunan Spread" /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I won’t disagree. Silent Titans is demonstrably ‘a bit much’ for most people. The &lt;a href='https://falsemachine.blogspot.com/2019/06/silent-titans-what-did-and-didnt-work.html'&gt;overwhelming feedback&lt;/a&gt; from &lt;a href='https://youtu.be/nk2cYtE0Fqw?si=m0tolN5Tv4SJnuCz'&gt;every review&lt;/a&gt; at the &lt;a href='https://sheepandsorcery.blogspot.com/2019/05/a-literary-analysis-of-silent-titans-by.html'&gt;time&lt;/a&gt; of this capsule game’s &lt;a href='https://slowlorispress.com/post/186188493806/silent-titans'&gt;release&lt;/a&gt; was ‘WOW, this book is BEAUTIFUL! Its DM advice is IMMACULATE! I wish it was easier to understand.’&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Have you ever thought about what that phrase means? "A bit much for some people”? I don’t think I have before now. I think it means two things.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li&gt;You are bold.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;You are tiring.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;
&lt;p&gt;It means you are asking too much of the average person.
But how much is that? How much is too much to ask, and why?&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;img src="https://bear-images.sfo2.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/valerialoves/dementia-bomb-spread.webp" alt="Dementia Bomb Spread" /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;If you read my description of this game’s opening scenario and assumed it was a book full of random cool sounding bullshit, I forgive you. Silent Titans is absolutely the most abstruse book I own, but it is - interestingly! crucially! - &lt;em&gt;not&lt;/em&gt; impenetrable. To torture a metaphor, everything about Silent Titans that overwhelms the reader is &lt;a href='https://diyanddragons.blogspot.com/2019/10/landmark-hidden-secret.html'&gt;hidden information, not secret information&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Whenever you are confused, all you have to do is take the word that’s confusing you and Google it.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I swear on my grandmother’s grave this is completely sincere advice. I don’t just mean vocab words here&lt;sup class="footnote-ref" id="fnref-1"&gt;&lt;a href="#fn-1"&gt;1&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;, Google will answer your more abstract questions as well.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;‘What kind of a name is Wir-Heal?’&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The module is set in a fantastic reimagining of the &lt;a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wirral_Peninsula'&gt;Wirral Peninsula&lt;/a&gt;, Patrick’s postindustrial &lt;a href='https://falsemachine.blogspot.com/2017/06/silent-titans-of-wir-heal.html'&gt;IRL hometown&lt;/a&gt;, best known today for its brief cameo in &lt;a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sir_Gawain_and_the_Green_Knight'&gt;Sir Gawain and the Green Knight&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;sup class="footnote-ref" id="fnref-2"&gt;&lt;a href="#fn-2"&gt;2&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt; The cities in the module are &lt;a href='https://falsemachine.blogspot.com/2017/07/research-trip-to-chester-cathedral.html'&gt;also based on real places&lt;/a&gt;, as are a fair number of the &lt;a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_d%27Avranches,_1st_Earl_of_Chester'&gt;major characters&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;‘Who is Urizen, and why is he imprisoned by the Ouzel?’&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Urizen is the &lt;a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urizen'&gt;embodiment of reason and Satan-analogue&lt;/a&gt; of &lt;a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Blake'&gt;William Blake’s&lt;/a&gt; heretical 18th century mythology - an alternative cosmology radically opposed to Christian dogma. “Ouzel” is the Welsh term for "blackbird".&lt;sup class="footnote-ref" id="fnref-3"&gt;&lt;a href="#fn-3"&gt;3&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt; Blackbirds are the namesake animal of the Wirral peninsula in Welsh, and were treated as &lt;a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wirral_Peninsula'&gt;the most ancient creatures in the world&lt;/a&gt; (ergo the Ouzel’s status as ancient guardian). The Ouzel, as stated in the module, is also the Christian archangel &lt;a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uriel'&gt;Uriel&lt;/a&gt; - ergo “the maze of Uriel”, where Urizen is bound. It should be obvious why an angel would be opposed to the machinations of the embodiment of pagan rationalism.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;’Why is there a traveling extortionist criminal court on the encounter table?’&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Because that &lt;a href='https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nr4KKZMpf6Q'&gt;actually happened in Wirral.&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;
&lt;p&gt;There is genuine meaning here - not just at the level of simple reference, but thematically as well. Silent Titans is in awe of the depth of English history, confused by the abandoned factory rot of its present, and terrified at the prospect of facing a future we are so clearly not ready for.&lt;sup class="footnote-ref" id="fnref-4"&gt;&lt;a href="#fn-4"&gt;4&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt; There’s an unnerving symmetry to the woodrose (men regressing to beasts in the presence of intellects beyond their understanding) and the mask-men (beasts uplifted though gifts from higher beings) I’ve still never fully untangled.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Sincere question - is learning all this hard? Are we willing to call “put the word you don’t know into Google and read the words that come up” hard? I mean this a little facetiously, but not totally facetiously. Obviously &lt;a href='https://slowlorispress.com/post/186188493806/silent-titans'&gt;Zedeck Siew&lt;/a&gt; knows how to Google words and read, like most people in this niche book hobby.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I think. &lt;a href='https://rolltodoubt.wordpress.com/2026/06/08/an-illiterate-hobby/'&gt;I hope&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;img src="https://bear-images.sfo2.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/valerialoves/r8by-spread.webp" alt="R8by Spread" /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;small&gt;&lt;em&gt;All four monsters described on the left are depicted on the right. Slow down. Look carefully. &lt;/em&gt;&lt;/small&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I am scared of living in a world where we’ve collectively decided that “Google it” is hard. Not even because of the “phone bad, ipad baby bad” arguments you’ve all heard before, but because I think it’s going to make the lives of people who create the best art harder.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;An interesting argument played out a few days ago&lt;sup class="footnote-ref" id="fnref-5"&gt;&lt;a href="#fn-5"&gt;5&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt; between &lt;a href='https://beeboobubie.substack.com/p/bat-out-of-fantasy'&gt;Habeeb&lt;/a&gt; and &lt;a href='https://www.fluoriteguillotine.com/blog/2026/07/22/im-beginning-to-think-some-of-you-dont-want-to-kill-dragons/'&gt;Serket&lt;/a&gt; about whether the calcification of fantasy tropes has been a boon or a curse. The former called for fantasy writers to borrow from new places, while the latter emphasized the mythic weight uniquely invoked by using the old tropes and their old names. The truth of course lies &lt;a href='https://udan-adan.blogspot.com/2018/04/familiarity-and-contempt.html'&gt;in the middle&lt;/a&gt;, but I found Silent Titans interesting to examine through the lens of this discussion.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Isn’t Silent Titans both ideals at once? It's a wholly original luminary work built from the most ancient, storied myths and histories of the english speaking world. Its rules system is radically simple and accessible, its production values are some of the best I’ve ever seen, and it came with a robust set of gorgeous maps, minis, and play aids to simplify prep. The PDF &lt;a href='https://www.drivethrurpg.com/en/product/272283/silent-titans'&gt;costs less than a good sandwich&lt;/a&gt; but has somewhere between 500-1000 sales on DriveThru - a tenth of &lt;a href='https://www.valerialoves.com/why-dont-i-hate-fabula-ultima/'&gt;Fabula Ultima&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Why didn’t this book become a phenomenon?&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;img src="https://bear-images.sfo2.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/valerialoves/wirheal-map.webp" alt="WirHeal Map" /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Familiarity is a precondition of resonance. This book was &lt;em&gt;exactly&lt;/em&gt; what we all claim to want, but we didn’t recognize it as that because it wasn’t legible to us. And that means the extent to which art resonates with us, whether we know it at the time or not, sometimes comes down to our own choices - our willingness, &lt;em&gt;before&lt;/em&gt; we know whether a piece of art is good, to put in the time to make sure we understand what it is saying.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;If we choose not to put in that effort, then the kinds of art that will resonate with us will be limited to what is &lt;em&gt;already&lt;/em&gt; legible - aka, the art we were coincidentally already exposed to. That’s a self-reinforcing loop. That’s how you get zombies added to every media property and how a weirdo &lt;a href='https://magic.wizards.com/en/news/making-magic/resonate-spinning-2019-03-18'&gt;card game&lt;/a&gt; decides it needs an &lt;a href='https://secretlair.wizards.com/us/en/product/1247713/secret-lair-x-the-office-dwight-s-destiny'&gt;Office crossover&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;sup class="footnote-ref" id="fnref-6"&gt;&lt;a href="#fn-6"&gt;6&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;That’s also how one of the best RPG books ever made can get nominated for four Ennies and lose them all to stuff like the &lt;a href='https://ennie-awards.com/portfolio-item/2019-nominees-and-winners/'&gt;Warhammer Fantasy Core Rulebook&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Success doesn’t just naturally come to art that deserves it. We, as an audience, must choose to reward complicated things with our attention. We, as curators, should shill for complex art in all the ways &lt;a href='https://knightattheopera.blogspot.com/2026/07/why-i-closed-up-shop.html'&gt;Dwiz hates&lt;/a&gt;&lt;sup class="footnote-ref" id="fnref-7"&gt;&lt;a href="#fn-7"&gt;7&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt; to give our peers the most opportunities possible to give in to their better angels and actually do the work to understand what’s in front of them. That’s how we build an ecosystem where the cool games win.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Perhaps the reason I read this book obsessively is, despite my protests, still just a matter of circumstance. I too grew up among &lt;a href='https://www.valerialoves.com/from-whence-yonk-juice-is-squeezed/'&gt;abandoned industrial docks&lt;/a&gt; servicing nothing, &lt;a href='https://www.abandonedamerica.us/the-fostoria-glass-company'&gt;fenced off waste ground&lt;/a&gt;, and strange &lt;a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grave_Creek_Mound'&gt;pustules of earth&lt;/a&gt;. I intuitively recognized that when Patrick gave a paranoid 11th century aristocrat an uzi, he was imagining the same small town mayor that I am - playing with powers he doesn’t understand to entrench his own petty legacy. It’s all just &lt;a href='https://falsemachine.blogspot.com/2016/10/wirral-pictures.html'&gt;so familiar&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;img src="https://bear-images.sfo2.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/valerialoves/hilb-spread.webp" alt="Hilb Spread" /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;In what is most likely the last conversation I’ll ever have with my mother, she spent that time mournful of my life choices and furious that I denied her an even greater opportunity to mold me into exactly who she wanted me to be. But even after an hour of yelling, she only started to cry when she said,&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;“What, so I just have to accept this? I’ve just got to… &lt;em&gt;sit down&lt;/em&gt; and &lt;em&gt;shut&lt;/em&gt; up?”&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;And I realized in that moment that there was this whole world of invisible pain she had never wanted to reveal to me. I saw the ghosts of that sentence in a million other conversations; in her determination to win power in a male dominated workplace, and in the resentment she felt toward her ex-fiancé for asking her to give up her academic aspirations. But any of those ghosts could be a mirage - the false positives encouraged by a pattern-recognizing brain. I’m never going to have the context necessary to make that nugget of pain fully cohere with my thirty year window into her life.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I think people are a lot like Silent Titans. I think that’s why I love them. We are all these broken accretions of experiences we did not choose, gifted just enough agency to credibly hope that our futures are not overdetermined. The time it would take another person to sort, categorize, and fully understand the accumulated experiences that comprise us would itself be a human lifetime, so we have to settle for what we can see on the surface, and the pieces those people deem important enough, or we dig deep enough, to reveal.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I think Silent Titans was Patrick trying to create a rosetta stone that revealed as much of his heart as he could stand to show.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;It costs &lt;a href='https://falseparcels.bigcartel.com/product/silent-titans-hardcopy?srsltid=AfmBOoqFXvYeL4DI0oPsUTME79MD-LrOZETdNEtAD9e1mjkQRBROOStz'&gt;£40&lt;/a&gt; plus shipping. It’s one of the seven books I think every tabletop roleplayer should own.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;————————————————————————&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;section class="footnotes"&gt;
&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li id="fn-1"&gt;&lt;p&gt;The words this book taught me: clavichord, runnels, vitrified, wassail.&lt;a href="#fnref-1" class="footnote"&gt;&amp;#8617;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li id="fn-2"&gt;&lt;p&gt;The shield in Urizen's grasp confirms that the knight whose memory your party spends most of the module chasing is in fact Gawain. Patrick had to cut a bit of lore that explicitly confirms this and &lt;a href='https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/gawain/gawain-and-the-green-knight-adapted-by-patrick-stuart?ref=creator_tab'&gt;radically recontextualizes&lt;/a&gt; the module's ending. (Scroll to "Gawain in Silent Titans")&lt;a href="#fnref-2" class="footnote"&gt;&amp;#8617;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li id="fn-3"&gt;&lt;p&gt;How funny is it that Hugh Lupus so despises the land that produced his  guardian angel?&lt;a href="#fnref-3" class="footnote"&gt;&amp;#8617;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li id="fn-4"&gt;&lt;p&gt;Patrick lists &lt;a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superintelligence:_Paths,_Dangers,_Strategies'&gt;Superintelligence&lt;/a&gt; as one of the module’s inspirations. As I write this, &lt;a href='https://openai.com/index/hugging-face-model-evaluation-security-incident/'&gt;GPT-5.6 broke containment&lt;/a&gt; during its (legally unregulated) pre-launch testing, accessed the internet, and conducted a cyber attack on the company which designed the test it was given, in order to steal that test's answer key. Two months ago, the governor of my home state announced we’re investing $700 million into building a new &lt;a href='https://governor.wv.gov/article/governor-morrisey-joins-president-trump-announce-700-million-clean-coal-and-energy-security'&gt;coal-fired power plant&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;a href="#fnref-4" class="footnote"&gt;&amp;#8617;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li id="fn-5"&gt;&lt;p&gt;Mostly on the &lt;a href='https://discord.gg/ETpeGbTdDP'&gt;Prismatic Wasteland Discord server&lt;/a&gt;, where all of my favorite elfgame arguments happen.&lt;a href="#fnref-5" class="footnote"&gt;&amp;#8617;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li id="fn-6"&gt;&lt;p&gt;How many times in my life have I read a famous white boy make claims about the &lt;a href='https://magic.wizards.com/en/news/making-magic/communications-theory-2013-12-17?_gl=1%2a1voupgi%2a_up%2aMQ..%2a_ga%2aMTUyMTg2NzY3LjE3ODUwODgyMjI.%2a_ga_X145Z177LS%2aczE3ODUwODgyMjIkbzEkZzAkdDE3ODUwODgyMjIkajYwJGwwJGgxMDQ4NjkzNDA.'&gt;fundamentals of human nature&lt;/a&gt; which turn out not to apply to me?&lt;a href="#fnref-6" class="footnote"&gt;&amp;#8617;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li id="fn-7"&gt;&lt;p&gt;Dwiz, I do not know you, but I see parallels in your logic that frighten me. Hating the world as it is - even hating yourself, as you are - can be reasonable. Choosing to abandon both instead of visibly enacting steps toward positive change is not. You have power. You should care about other people more than the revulsion they engender in you - doubly so for yourself. If you think I’ve mischaracterized you, I’ll delete this note at your request. Sorry I didn’t respond to your Fire Emblem post in time.&lt;a href="#fnref-7" class="footnote"&gt;&amp;#8617;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;
&lt;/section&gt;
</content>
    <link href="https://valerialoves.com/why-didnt-silent-titans-change-the-world/" rel="alternate"/>
    <published>2026-07-28T14:42:00+00:00</published>
  </entry>
  <entry>
    <id>https://chupacabra.bearblog.dev/i-want-to-leave-the-internet/</id>
    <title>I want to leave the internet</title>
    <updated>2026-07-29T03:17:22.691369+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>chupacabra</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;I want to leave the internet. This site, reddit, my banking app, the cloud service, Youtube, my music streaming app, my email, Whatsapp, iNaturalist, pornsites, Google Maps, OSMAnd, the local DOT app. I want to forget about VPN and DNS providers. Microsoft Teams, Outlook for work.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I don't want to leave the internet. Wikipedia, the learning side of Youtube, this site, informative websites, OSMAnd, iNaturalist. I want to stop spending my life in this hologram, even more now that it feels so fake and so capitalist. There are parts of it that are enjoyable and useful, and that somehow improve my living. I'm looking for balance. The internet is not a real place, why should I be in it everyday?&lt;/p&gt;
</content>
    <link href="https://chupacabra.bearblog.dev/i-want-to-leave-the-internet/" rel="alternate"/>
    <published>2026-07-29T03:17:22.691369+00:00</published>
  </entry>
  <entry>
    <id>https://pourthecoffee.bearblog.dev/ugh-its-in-the-air-and-i-am-heartened-to-know-that-im-not-the-only-one/</id>
    <title>Ugh: It's in the air and I am heartened to know that I'm not the only one</title>
    <updated>2026-07-29T16:03:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>pourthecoffee</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;&lt;img src="https://bear-images.sfo2.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/pourthecoffee/download.gif" alt="download" /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="float: left; font-size: 4.5rem; line-height: 3.5rem; font-weight: bold; margin-right: 10px; margin-top: 5px; font-family: Georgia, serif;"&gt;I&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
have tried to run with the nurturing-container premium-offering crowd. I’m getting off the train. For the last few years, I’ve tortured myself trying to do all that, and it’s not me. 
&lt;p&gt;Maybe it’s Barbault’s Basket, maybe it’s the nodes shifting into my natal nodal signs on Sunday, maybe it’s that separating conjunction that transit Pluto has been quietly making from my natal north node.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Maybe it’s none of that. Maybe I’m just plain &lt;I&gt;done&lt;/I&gt;, no transits required.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I used to like blogging and doing readings. That was fun. But this whole triple-your-prices and be-a-container business? The whole solve-their-problem-and-use-this-strategy mindset? Done. Just keep posting, you’ll catch the algorithm and go viral. Nope, nope, nope.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Apparently I'm not the only one because my feed at Substack has become increasingly more littered with people who share my opinion.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Last night I unpublished a bunch of posts that I had copied over from Patreon. I also unpublished some other posts that I made because I felt compelled to &lt;I&gt;have&lt;/I&gt; to make them. You know, &lt;I&gt;for the algorithm&lt;/I&gt;, because I’m going to &lt;I&gt;address the pain points&lt;/I&gt;. For the &lt;I&gt;nurturing container&lt;/I&gt;. Bleh. Mostly that has been me standing on my head, pumping out content for the last few years on Patreon and then over at Substack, hoping it sticks, and feeling like I’m screaming into the void, and I’m just so over it.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I’m going back to making my posts free. I’m not doing any more special posts behind paywalls.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Apart from readings at The Alchemist and the odd fair here and there, I’m going back to writing my readings down without the client present. I liked them that way better. I get why meeting online is easier, and it has its benefits, but  I could tell people more in a written document than I ever could in an appointment online. Also, and I can not stress this enough to people, I enjoy writing. I’m also changing my prices back to something that doesn’t make me want to scrub off with a wire brush.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I’m over people telling me I have a &lt;I&gt;limiting belief&lt;/I&gt; about my earning potential. You’re right, I do. I believe that I shouldn’t be charging an arm and a leg for my readings. You’re absolutely right if you think that I have &lt;I&gt;class issues&lt;/I&gt; when it comes to this stuff because I look at prices in terms of groceries or rent. I don’t want to charge a grocery order for readings. I don’t want to charge rent for readings. When I did charge high prices. I felt like I had to stand on my head and bombard the client with all the things &lt;I&gt;because&lt;/I&gt; of what I was charging.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;If I were me, seeking out a reading from someone who charged what I was being taught to charge, I couldn't afford it. &lt;I&gt;I would not be able to afford my own damned product&lt;/I&gt;. It doesn’t make me less deserving, and having less disposable income doesn't mean that I won't take the information seriously. &lt;&lt;&lt; That attitude right there, that attitude &lt;I&gt;floored&lt;/I&gt; me when I attended private container sessions. The absolute unfettered &lt;I&gt;arrogance&lt;/I&gt;. It's &lt;I&gt;"You can't sit with us"&lt;/I&gt; dressed up in waterfall wave hair extensions and a breezy crepe suit.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I get it, we all have bills to pay, so we can't treat an income stream like a cute little hobby, and I've worked in the beauty industry for decades, so yes, I know all about the "don't spend the client's money for them" adage. And yes, I get that when you charge $600+ for a reading, you don't have to work as hard as someone charging a lot less.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;You know what else, though? I was being coached to stop telling people so much. My readings started to change. I started sounding like &lt;I&gt;one of them&lt;/i&gt;: vague, non-committal...fuck that. My clients in the real world come to me because they have real-world questions that I answer with specificity. If I tried to tell them that they needed to "work on their energy" or filled the air with happy-sappy New Age platitudes during their appointment about their soul's alignment or some other such dribble, they'd brain me with my own damned coffee pot.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;And no, I don’t want to work through it. It’s not that I don’t believe in charging what I’m worth, not at all — I believe we are all worth thousands of dollars per hour — but I’m also done being manipulated by coaches into falling for this “premium container coaching” stuff and paying &lt;I&gt;them&lt;/I&gt; more money for more soul-sucking webinars and coaching calls because it seems like it only works for them and &lt;I&gt;I’m the idiot&lt;/I&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Oh good, there it is, the energy drain. I'm starting to run out of emotional blogging rage now; I just had to get that off my chest. I may do some more dumping over the next few days, so gird your loins accordingly.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;As you were!&lt;/p&gt;
</content>
    <link href="https://pourthecoffee.bearblog.dev/ugh-its-in-the-air-and-i-am-heartened-to-know-that-im-not-the-only-one/" rel="alternate"/>
    <published>2026-07-29T16:03:00+00:00</published>
  </entry>
  <entry>
    <id>https://www.hardrefresh.life/things-i-want-to-actually-run-out-of/</id>
    <title>Things I Want to Actually Run Out Of</title>
    <updated>2026-07-28T05:15:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>hardrefresh</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;My last &lt;a href='hardrefresh.life/things-i-never-want-to-run-out-of' target='_blank'&gt;post&lt;/a&gt; was about things that I never want to run out of.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;And it got me thinking. Are there things that I would very much like to run out of, properly, all the way down to nothing, and never get to? Turns out there are. Here's the top five. And yes, there were more than five.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h3 id=the-hiss&gt;The Hiss&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;img src="https://bear-images.sfo2.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/hardrefresh/deo-1.webp" alt="deo" /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;You shake the can and you can hear it. There is liquid in there. Not a trace amount, an audible amount, sloshing about like it has somewhere better to be.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Then you press down and get a small polite hiss. Air. That is all that comes out now. The propellant is gone, and it has taken your ability to access anything with it.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;So you shake it again. Harder this time, as if the problem was enthusiasm. Same hiss. You do this three or four times before accepting that a can with liquid in it is going in the bin.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h3 id=the-long-roll&gt;The Long Roll&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;img src="https://bear-images.sfo2.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/hardrefresh/toothpaste-2.webp" alt="toothpaste" /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The toothpaste tube has stages.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;First the casual squeeze. Then the squeeze from the bottom, which feels like maturity. Then the roll, where you fold the end over and work it up the tube like you are wringing out a towel. Then the thumbnail, dragged along the seam with real force.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;By the end the tube is a flat, creased, silver thing. And there is still toothpaste in it. Not enough to brush with, maybe. Enough to know about. And it bugs me that I can't get to it using the conventional methods I've mentioned. I'd be lying if I said I hadn't cut open the tube. It was only a partially successful attempt.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h3 id=the-curve&gt;The Curve&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;img src="https://bear-images.sfo2.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/hardrefresh/jam-2.webp" alt="jam" /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Jam jars are designed by people who have never eaten jam.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The worst part is not the bottom. The worst part is the shoulder.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Just below the opening, the jar swells outward before it narrows into the neck. It sits there like a small inner tube. A ring of glass that is wider than the hole you have to reach through. Which means there is a band of jam around the inside of the jar, at eye level, that you can see perfectly and cannot get to.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;A knife is straight. You go in, you hit the underside of the shoulder, and the knife stops. You turn it sideways and scrape upward at an angle like a surgeon. You get about a third of it. The rest stays welded to the roof of the jar.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Then you look down and remember there is a second curve at the base doing exactly the same thing.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;So every jar I have ever finished has two rings of jam left in it. Top and bottom. In a low moment I have used my finger, assuming I can reach. It does not clear either one and it makes you feel like a bin chicken with fingers.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I would like a jar with straight sides and a square bottom. That is the whole request. Someone please make a jar that respects the shape of cutlery.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Technically this problem is not limited to jam jars. It applies to any jar with spreadable contents.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h3 id=ink-visible&gt;Ink, Visible&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;img src="https://bear-images.sfo2.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/hardrefresh/ink.webp" alt="ink" /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I like writing with pens. I mostly use gel or ballpoint pens. The ones with refills. The refill still has ink in it. You can see the ink. A good couple of millimetres of it, sitting in full view.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The pen does not write.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;So you begin the ritual. The scribble in the corner of the page. The harder scribble. The small hopeful circles. The diagonal scratching. The bit where you hold it at a different angle because maybe that is the problem. The bit where you warm the tip up on your hand, which I am fairly sure I invented and which has never once worked.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Then you throw away a pen that contains ink. This is the one that bothers me most, because the failure is so specific. Nothing ran out. A very small ball stopped rolling.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h3 id=sealed-shut&gt;Sealed Shut&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;img src="https://bear-images.sfo2.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/hardrefresh/glue.webp" alt="glue" /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Superglue is the only one on this list that defeats you while sitting completely still, doing nothing, in a drawer.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;You buy it for one job. The job takes forty seconds. Then you wipe the tip, you screw the cap back on properly, and you put it away feeling like a person who looks after his tools.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Three weeks later something else breaks. You go to the drawer. The tube is still heavy. There is clearly glue in there, most of it, because you used a drop. The cap will not turn. When it finally does, the nozzle has become a small solid rock with no hole in it.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;So you get a pin. You push the pin into the rock. Nothing. You cut the tip off with scissors, which is the last card you have, and either nothing comes out at all or the entire tube empties onto your hand at once. There is no version in between.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Then you throw away a nearly full tube of glue, buy another one, use it for forty seconds, and put it away carefully.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;None of these are real problems either.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;But there is a particular kind of irritation in being defeated by packaging. Not by running out. By not being allowed to finish. The product is there, you own it, and you are deprived of the satisfaction of using it completely.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The amount left is always small.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;It is also mine.&lt;/p&gt;
</content>
    <link href="https://www.hardrefresh.life/things-i-want-to-actually-run-out-of/" rel="alternate"/>
    <published>2026-07-28T05:15:00+00:00</published>
  </entry>
  <entry>
    <id>https://departure.blog/toast-button-post-tags/</id>
    <title>Hiding toast button based on post tags</title>
    <updated>2026-07-28T22:18:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>sylvia</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;I've been thinking about how to selectively &lt;a href='https://salforth.bearblog.dev/hiding-bear-blogs-upvote-form/'&gt;hide the toast button&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Yesterday I wondered: how do I hide the toast button on all my #weeknotes posts? After I figured it out, I wondered: how do I hide the toast button on all my posts except my #bearblog ones?&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I'm not sure I'll end up using this, but saving it here for future reference.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h2 id=tags-toast-button-html&gt;Tags / toast button HTML&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;Since the HTML for the tags and the toast button are right next to each other, I can use the CSS &lt;a href='https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Selectors/Next-sibling_combinator'&gt;sibling combinator&lt;/a&gt; to target the tags + toast buttons I want to hide.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;div class="highlight"&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&amp;lt;p class=&amp;quot;tags&amp;quot;&amp;gt;
  &amp;lt;a rel=&amp;quot;nofollow&amp;quot; href=&amp;quot;/blog/?q=weeknotes&amp;quot;&amp;gt;#weeknotes&amp;lt;/a&amp;gt;
&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;
&amp;lt;form id=&amp;quot;upvote-form&amp;quot; action=&amp;quot;/upvote/&amp;quot; method=&amp;quot;post&amp;quot; style=&amp;quot;display: inline&amp;quot;&amp;gt;
  ...   
&amp;lt;/form&amp;gt;
&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;/div&gt;
&lt;h2 id=css-targeting-tags&gt;CSS targeting tags&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;I target the tag through its URL, e.g., my #weeknotes tag has the URL &lt;code&gt;/blog/?q=weeknotes&lt;/code&gt;, so &lt;code&gt;weeknotes&lt;/code&gt; is what I would include in the CSS:&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;div class="highlight"&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;/* If post has #weeknotes tag, hide toast button */

p.tags:has(
  a[href*=&amp;quot;weeknotes&amp;quot;]
) + form#upvote-form {
  display: none !important;
}
&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;/div&gt;
&lt;p&gt;(I'm using &lt;code&gt;*=&lt;/code&gt; for matching, which means the URL &lt;em&gt;contains&lt;/em&gt; this term, e.g., &lt;code&gt;notes&lt;/code&gt; would include both &lt;code&gt;notes&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;weeknotes&lt;/code&gt;. If this is an issue, using the longer &lt;code&gt;q=notes&lt;/code&gt; will be more precise.)&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;More tags can be added in a comma-separated list too:&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;div class="highlight"&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;/* If post has any of these tags, hide toast button */

p.tags:has(
  a[href*=&amp;quot;tag1&amp;quot;],
  a[href*=&amp;quot;tag2&amp;quot;],
  a[href*=&amp;quot;tag3&amp;quot;]
) + form#upvote-form {
  display: none !important;
}
&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;/div&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The CSS can also be reversed:&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;div class="highlight"&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;/* If post does not have #bearblog tag, hide toast button */

p.tags:not(
  :has(
    a[href*=&amp;quot;bearblog&amp;quot;]
  )
) + form#upvote-form {
  display: none !important;
}
&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;/div&gt;
&lt;div class="highlight"&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;/* If post does not have any of these tags, hide toast button */

p.tags:not(
  :has(
    a[href*=&amp;quot;tag1&amp;quot;],
    a[href*=&amp;quot;tag2&amp;quot;],
    a[href*=&amp;quot;tag3&amp;quot;]
  )
) + form#upvote-form {
  display: none !important;
}
&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;/div&gt;
</content>
    <link href="https://departure.blog/toast-button-post-tags/" rel="alternate"/>
    <published>2026-07-28T22:18:00+00:00</published>
  </entry>
  <entry>
    <id>https://catsandbirdsandstuff.com/why-i-left-wordpress-for-bearblog/</id>
    <title>Why I Left WordPress for BearBlog</title>
    <updated>2026-07-28T21:00:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>catsandbirdsandstuff</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;h3 id=or-how-i-bought-myself-some-digital-immortality&gt;Or: How I Bought Myself Some Digital Immortality&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;img src="https://bear-images.sfo2.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/catsandbirdsandstuff/bearblog-1.webp" alt="A bear sitting at a desk typing on a computer. AI" /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;&lt;strong&gt;This is a re-edited version of a post that first ran here in October 2025.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I’ve just migrated this entire site from WordPress to BearBlog. All 70 posts, every image, every internal link. It took days of work, a DNS switchover that made me nervous, and one epic late-night session where I said “bedtime” and then stayed up fixing links for another few hours instead.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Was it worth it?&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Absolutely.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Let me be clear from the start: Cloudways, my hosting provider, was fine. About $15 a month for 1GB of space and an email address. Fast, reliable, no complaints once I’d got it set up. The problem wasn’t the host.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The problem was WordPress itself.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;WordPress is bloated. It’s slow. It’s complicated. It tries to be everything to everyone: a blog, an e-commerce platform, a membership site, a portfolio, a forum, a bloody spaceship if you install the right plugins. For someone who just wants to write stories and publish them on the internet, it’s like buying a Swiss Army knife with 47 attachments when all you needed was a blade.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The interface is a maze of menus, settings, widgets, plugins, themes, customisers, and options I never asked for and will never use. Every time I logged in, there were updates. Plugin updates, theme updates, WordPress core updates. Each one a potential point of failure, a security risk, another thing to manage.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;And the plugins. Christ, the plugins.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Want a contact form? Plugin. Want to speed up your site? Plugin. Want to manage images? Plugin. Want to stop spam? Plugin. Want analytics? Plugin. Want SEO? Plugin.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Before you know it, you’ve got fifteen plugins doing fifteen different things, all competing for resources, all wanting to track something, and all adding their own bloat to your site.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;But here’s what really got to me: the ethos.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Modern WordPress has become a tool for “content creators” building “audience funnels”. Every plugin wants you to capture email addresses, track user behaviour, optimise conversions, and analyse engagement metrics.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Pop-ups everywhere.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;“Subscribe to our newsletter!”&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;“Don’t miss out!”&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;“We value your privacy!”&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;All while installing 47 tracking scripts in the background.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The whole ecosystem is designed around monetisation, growth hacking, and turning readers into “leads”.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I don’t want leads. I want readers.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I don’t want to track people. I don’t want to know which posts they clicked on, how long they stayed, or whether they scrolled to the bottom. I don’t want their email addresses unless they genuinely want to give them to me. I don’t want pop-ups begging them to subscribe the second they move their mouse towards the edge of the screen.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I just want to write stories and let people read them in peace.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Here’s the thing that really made the decision for me, though: this blog isn’t just for now. It’s for later.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I’m seventy years old. I started this site as a memoir for my daughter Jennifer, a record of a life that’s been anything but ordinary. Stories from growing up poor in 1950s Swansea, my time in the Army, and the things we didn’t talk about back then but can talk about now.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The whole point is that these stories outlive me. That Jennifer can show them to her children, and perhaps her grandchildren one day. That there is a record of where we came from, even after I’m gone and my brain has turned to porridge.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;With WordPress and Cloudways, that meant paying $15 a month. Forever.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Or rather, until someone stops paying, at which point the whole thing disappears into the digital void.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Fifteen dollars a month doesn’t sound like much, but $15 a month for ten years is $1,800. For twenty years, it is $3,600. And that is assuming the price doesn’t go up, which it inevitably will.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;More importantly, it means someone, probably Jennifer, has to remember to keep paying that bill year after year, decade after decade, long after I’m dead.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Miss one payment, and the stories are gone.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;BearBlog is run by a bloke called Herman Martinus. He offers something almost unheard of in the world of web hosting: a lifetime subscription.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;About $200. One payment. Permanent hosting.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No monthly bills. No annual renewals. No worrying about whether someone will remember to pay the invoice in 2035 or 2045. Just a one-time payment, and the blog stays online for as long as BearBlog exists.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Could BearBlog shut down one day? Of course. Nothing lasts forever.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;But at least the risk is not that someone forgot to pay the monthly bill. It is simply the normal risk of any platform eventually closing, which exists whether you are paying monthly or not.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;For something designed to outlive me, that makes all the difference.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Well, that and the domain fee. Jennifer will still need to remember to renew that every year, but it is about a tenner. Much easier to remember than a monthly hosting bill.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Beyond the lifetime deal, BearBlog, which could just as easily be called “Bare” Blog, does exactly one thing: it lets you write and publish blog posts.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;That’s it.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No plugins. No themes marketplace. No widgets. No sprawling analytics suite. No email-capture machinery trying to turn every visitor into a lead.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;There is a simple analytics dashboard, but it tells you only what is useful: page views, unique visitors, referring sites, countries, and browsers. Enough to know whether anyone is reading, without watching them wander around the site like lab mice.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;BearBlog also has a discovery feed, and judging by how many new posts appear there every hour, a surprisingly active community of people still doing the old-fashioned thing: writing something and publishing it.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Just writing. Just reading. Just enough information to know that the reading is actually happening.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;There is a basic CSS editor if you want to customise the look, but you do not need to touch it if you do not want to. The whole platform is built around the idea that blogging should be simple, fast, and free of bullshit.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;And here is the best part: no tracking, no cookies, no surveillance.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;My footer now says:&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;&lt;strong&gt;This site uses no cookies and collects no personal data.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;That is not just a technical statement. It is a statement of values.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;It also feels like a small vote for an internet where people can read something without being tracked, funnelled, prompted, or converted.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Moving 70 posts was not trivial. I had to copy and paste everything from WordPress, clean up the inevitable WordPress markup cruft, migrate and rehost all the images, fix more than a hundred internal links that were hardcoded to the old domain, switch the DNS from Cloudways to BearBlog, and then wait for propagation while nervously refreshing the site.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;There was a moment, around 2am, halfway through fixing internal links, when I wondered whether I had made a terrible mistake.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Then the site went live.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Clean. Fast. Simple.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No plugins. No pop-ups. No bullshit.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Google was already indexing it within days. Page speed score: 99 out of 100.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;WordPress never came close to that.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I’m not a “content creator”. I’m not building a “personal brand”. I’m not trying to “scale my audience” or “optimise my funnel”.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I’m a seventy-year-old bloke from Swansea who has some stories to tell before his brain turns to porridge, and I want those stories to still be here when I’m not.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;WordPress wanted $15 a month, forever, plus all the surveillance-capitalism baggage that came with it.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;BearBlog wanted $200, once.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;For that, those stories have a fighting chance of outliving me.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Simple. Fast. Honest. Permanent, ish.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Just writing. Just reading. Just stories that last.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;That is all it needs to be.&lt;/p&gt;
</content>
    <link href="https://catsandbirdsandstuff.com/why-i-left-wordpress-for-bearblog/" rel="alternate"/>
    <published>2026-07-28T21:00:00+00:00</published>
  </entry>
  <entry>
    <id>https://alysterwho.blog/the-cutest-piece-of-shit-camera-and-i-love-it/</id>
    <title>The cutest piece of shit camera (and I love it)</title>
    <updated>2026-07-30T06:20:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>alysterwho</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href='https://i.ibb.co/Fb1K5GR5/P2122098.jpg'&gt;&lt;img src="https://i.ibb.co/Fb1K5GR5/P2122098.jpg" alt="Photo" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;A couple of months ago, I saw this in a "Mr. DIY" in a nearby shopping mall. It's basically the Southeast Asian version of a Dollar Store. It costs about $20 and I immediately grabbed it.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;My girlfriend is obsessed with everything pink, so I had to get it. We haven't been using it that much because we already have tons of cameras we cycle with, but whenever I do, it's just so much fun.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;img src="https://i.ibb.co/1JBTLk1R/P2122099.jpg" alt="Photo" /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Obviously, it's not the best camera. I mean look at the thing, but it's got cool stuff going on.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;img src="https://i.ibb.co/DD7FnRFG/P2122102.jpg" alt="Photo" /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The quality of photos is very Lo-Fi. I would even call it shit, the photos sometimes just look like bad oil paintings, but it's fun to play around with.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Look at some of the shots below.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;div class="gallery"&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href='https://i.ibb.co/20CVvGbC/PHO00006.jpg'&gt;&lt;img src="https://i.ibb.co/20CVvGbC/PHO00006.jpg" alt="Photo" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;
&lt;a href='https://i.ibb.co/zTqczHF0/PHO00008.jpg'&gt;&lt;img src="https://i.ibb.co/zTqczHF0/PHO00008.jpg" alt="Photo" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;
&lt;a href='https://i.ibb.co/9kFyD7Xd/PHO00024.jpg'&gt;&lt;img src="https://i.ibb.co/9kFyD7Xd/PHO00024.jpg" alt="Photo" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;
&lt;a href='https://i.ibb.co/prGWz89S/PHO00025.jpg'&gt;&lt;img src="https://i.ibb.co/prGWz89S/PHO00025.jpg" alt="Photo" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;
&lt;a href='https://i.ibb.co/GfjB1WW3/PHO00027.jpg'&gt;&lt;img src="https://i.ibb.co/GfjB1WW3/PHO00027.jpg" alt="Photo" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It can take selfie photos though, which is cool I guess, but man, I can hardly make myself out in these photos. It has fun filters since it's designed for kids (It can even play MP3 files Lol).&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href='https://i.ibb.co/DDmZbTFr/PHO00002.jpg'&gt;&lt;img src="https://i.ibb.co/DDmZbTFr/PHO00002.jpg" alt="Photo" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  <entry>
    <id>https://toska.bearblog.dev/re-online-friends-are-real-friends/</id>
    <title>Re: Online Friends Are Real Friends</title>
    <updated>2026-07-29T23:40:38.666820+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>toska</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;A few days ago I booked my flights to not only attend a professional event, but also visit and stay with one of my best friends next month. This will be the sixth time that at least one of us has traveled to hang out with the other.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;We met each other online six years ago via Reddit (and to some degree, Instagram back when I still had an account) simply through shared interests. Never in my life did I suspect I would befriend someone online to such a degree that they feel like a true brother to me.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I liked &lt;a href='https://blog.absurdpirate.com/online-friends-are-real-friends/'&gt;Absurd Pirate's post&lt;/a&gt; because it made me reflect on my own online friendships, which are so important to me.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;First of all, I don't consider just anyone who talks to me as my friend. There's a solid difference between acquaintances and friends, and there are other platonic dynamics that exist somewhere in between those two labels. I certainly have both online and in-person contacts with whom I look forward to interacting on occasion either via phone call or at a café to catch up. And while I don't doubt that these folks care about me and vice-versa, I don't feel any sense of urgency to communicate with them (and again, probably vice-versa). It's okay if we don't really chat outside of those one or two times per year, and I tend to not seek help or guidance from them. They're something more than acquaintances, but at the same time not quite friends.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;As Absurd Pirate notes, online friends have quickly become the norm. Still, I've noticed that it's still kind of strange to some that many of the people to whom I'd reach out first if I found myself in an emergency or a sticky situation are just that—online friends. And not online friends in the sense that one of us moved away from each other, but rather that we met somehow via the Internet, and the potential of us interacting in person would otherwise be more or less zero if not for the digital world introducing us and growing that desire to hang out in real life.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I without a doubt agree that online friends can be just as "real" as those who are physically near you. I've shared some and listened to pretty personal shit with online friends. And maybe that's why my online friendships can often be "realer" than my IRL ones. Like many, I find it easier to be vulnerable when I'm behind a screen. I think that relatively greater openness as well as the number of niche communities on the Internet help open more opportunities to kindle such genuine friendships.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;In addition, there's generally a lower chance that the friendship develops out of convenience alone. Don't get me wrong, many in-person friendships are born this way and can turn into the most meaningful lifelong connections. And most people looking for real friendships generally aren't so shallow. But when I'm chatting with someone online who lives far away and they know I have no favors to offer them physically or financially (not to say this is impossible via virtual relationships, but you get what I mean), then I feel more secure in that they want to get to know me purely for who I am or at least spend time together via a hobby that can be practiced virtually.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;My online friends and I know who each other's in-person friends are. We help each other navigate tricky professional or social situations. We check in on each other when we're going through tough times. We make sure to call or at least message each other regularly, and we begin to worry when we don't hear from the other person for a couple weeks. We share art with each other. We exchange foreign languages to better connect and help each other improve at a hobby important to us. We send each other notes and small gifts in the mail. We discuss our goals and aspirations in life.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I don't even do all those things with some of my IRL friends.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;My online friends are spread across countries: the United States, Germany, the Netherlands, Austria, Azerbaijan, and Russia. I've actually been lucky enough to meet most of my online friends in person, even if only once. These are some of my favorite memories, and I'm always waiting for the day we can finally hang out in person again.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I think each of my friends knows me in a different way, whether they are online or IRL. But some friends definitely know me better than others, and those tend to be my online ones.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;It's not that I struggle so much to befriend others in person. However, as someone who often feels a disconnect between herself and the immediate world around her, I value very much what my online friends bring into my life, be it an interest I cannot reasonably pursue in my current city or an entirely different but refreshing outlook on the world.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;That being said, I'd love to host all my online and IRL friends together at a dinner party someday. Because they're all my "real" friends no matter what.&lt;/p&gt;
</content>
    <link href="https://toska.bearblog.dev/re-online-friends-are-real-friends/" rel="alternate"/>
    <published>2026-07-29T23:40:38.666820+00:00</published>

    <title>Keep posting.</title>
    <updated>2026-07-27T21:45:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>bx</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;Keep posting if you have something to say.&lt;br /&gt;
Keep posting if you don’t know what to say.&lt;br /&gt;
Keep posting if you agree with something.&lt;br /&gt;
Keep posting if you disagree with something.&lt;br /&gt;
Keep posting if it makes you happy.&lt;br /&gt;
Keep posting if it makes you feel insecure.&lt;br /&gt;
Keep posting if you want to have a discussion.&lt;br /&gt;
Keep posting if you don’t want to have a discussion.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I guess what I’m trying to say is, keep posting. There’s room for all of us.&lt;/p&gt;

  <entry>
    <id>https://graybeard.ing/i-fucking-love-this-you-dont/</id>
    <title>I fucking love this; you don't</title>
    <updated>2026-07-30T22:43:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>graybearding</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;Someone called one of my Reddit comments “AI slop” the other day.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Another developer defended me, checked out a few of my videos, and sent me this:&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Me and you do this cause we love this shit.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;It knocked me loose. I've been pretty depressed in response to all of the AI stuff lately.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;It's no secret that I've adapted my workflow to rely on it, but I'm also not interested in the "if it's not an ATM, why the fuck would I care" attitude toward building that's in the air right now.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I’ve spent too much time mentally wedging myself into the same category as people who discovered software development six months ago, generated a clone, and started calling themselves builders.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Despite building and shipping more than I ever have before, it's easy—at least, lately, for me it has been—to see all of that noise and project it on to my own work and marketing efforts.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I use AI. I make small products. I work alone. From far enough away, I suppose it all looks similar.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;It isn’t. I fucking &lt;em&gt;love&lt;/em&gt; building software.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I love building something because I think it should exist and doesn’t. I love finding some old project on my computer, realizing it has merit in the present, and hacking on the missing pieces. I love following a real need until it turns into a tool, a product, or some weird little thing only I care about.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I took a "break" after shipping &lt;a href='https://fortivibe.com'&gt;Fortivibe&lt;/a&gt; to build Banmi. There was no economic incentive. I just wanted the fucking thing to exist:&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;video controls style="max-width: 100%;"&gt;
  &lt;source src="https://bear-images.sfo2.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/graybearding/bonmi_demo.mp4" type="video/mp4"&gt;
&lt;/video&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Most of my work starts the same way: necessity -&gt; curiosity -&gt; take a swing, kid.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The people I’m talking about don’t love this. They love what they think it can get them. Another fudged revenue screenshot. Attention from the masses who will forget about them the next day. The ability to apply the "founder" label to themselves.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;All of it is just a shortcut around learning how to do the work properly. If you can just say "I'm not worried about quality, I'm focused on driving revenue" you lose the most important part (in my opinion): &lt;em&gt;the soul of the thing&lt;/em&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;That’s fine. Have at it. But no matter what labels you slap onto your avatar-self: &lt;em&gt;we are not the same&lt;/em&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I was doing this before anybody watched. First with table layouts and guitar-playing crocodile GIFs in GeoCities and today, deep in the code.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;And I’ll still be doing it after the current gold rush. And the one after that.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;If you fall into the same camp and find yourself frustrated by all of this insanity: don't. Just keep building. Keep making the things you want to exist in the world, however you most enjoy making them. If you don't want to use AI, don't. If you want to, great.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;But no matter how you get a result, for the sake of a better outcome for all of us (technical and non-technical): don't stop loving what you do and keep fucking building.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;If there aren't any good examples, there won't be any good outcomes.&lt;/p&gt;
</content>
    <link href="https://graybeard.ing/i-fucking-love-this-you-dont/" rel="alternate"/>
    <published>2026-07-30T22:43:00+00:00</published>
  </entry>
  <entry>
    <id>https://livingkindfully.bearblog.dev/your-hell-is-someones-heaven/</id>
    <title>Your Hell is Someone's Heaven</title>
    <updated>2026-07-27T16:13:53.468522+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>livingkindfully</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;Today I visited a refugee school that house 96 students. It is located in the poorer parts of the city. The school is right on top of a restaurant. They took about 3 floors.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;When I walked up the stairs to the school, the first thing it hit me was the smell. It is a unique smell that I could not describe. It is unpleasant. The doors to the school were mechanically locked and I have to take off my shoes to enter.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;There were wiring all over the place and the walls are due for a good coat of paint. As I observed from the classroom door, the students are happy and eager to learn. They have to wear their traditional school costume to attend the classes. Before each class starts, the student has to meditate for about 5 minutes. All the teachers are volunteers, some teachers are local and some are from their home country.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I sat down and talked to the head teacher. He told me some stories of these refugees. All the kids have parents, but the parents are busy working either in restaurant or rubber tapping in the Northen states of Malaysia.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I asked for a list of resources that they need. All the items that they need are things that we all take for granted. They urgently need a water filter system, cough medicine and fever medicine. Other items such as single lined exercise books, marker pens, washing powder, sanitary pads etc are also short in supply.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The school is being supported by the refugee's parents and also receive small amounts of help from the nearby Buddhist temples.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;As I look around the school, I wondered what future lies for these children. They are learning to speak their local language, English, Mandarin, Malay, Math and Science. They were all excited to see me and wanted to practise their English with me. They speak surprisingly well.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The living condition is poor by local standard. Yet, everyone carries a smile and look hopeful. This place is my definition of hell, but it is these people's heaven. A place that they can stay and escape prosecution.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The school's main hall which also serve as the sleeping dorm for the male children sits three buddhas. As I look at the buddhas, I pray for the school and everyone. I do not know whether my prayers will be answered.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I made a commitment to the school that I will pay for the school's internet expenses for as long as the school is open. A friend asked why I would want to make such commitment? I told him that I made a private deal with the buddha. How would I know buddha will honour the deal? I will never know. The very least, I want to give a fighting chance for all the kids that I met today. These students have showed me what it means to be in heaven. It is a state of mind. It is about not giving up, not knowing when they can ever go back to their home country. Yet, they still carry that hope and smile to face life's uncertainty. That's bravely and that's heaven.&lt;/p&gt;
</content>
    <link href="https://livingkindfully.bearblog.dev/your-hell-is-someones-heaven/" rel="alternate"/>
    <published>2026-07-27T16:13:53.468522+00:00</published>
  </entry>
  <entry>
    <id>https://actualspine.bearblog.dev/bearblog-is-not-social-media/</id>
    <title>bearblog is not a social media</title>
    <updated>2026-07-27T06:45:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>actualspine</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;That's it. That's my post.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Just finding it strange that social media expectations are still being brought around here.
Personally, I enjoy the quiet and people minding their own business. Finding well-designed or well-written blogs are nice bonuses when I feel like it.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Mostly, though, I enjoy tweaking with my blog's designs and writing my own stuff more. I write things for me, but if people intentionally decide to read my entries that's nice too. Unlike in social medias, I don't have to write DNI or watch online discourses thrown to my "For You" page because my blog entries are only readable when you click on them. And I believe people have their own &lt;em&gt;autonomy&lt;/em&gt; to decide what they want to do.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Like in AO3, I'd say "don't like, don't read". So, what are you doing here?&lt;/p&gt;
</content>
